0.0.n: A neutral way to refer to yourself.

0.1.n: Marks わたし as the person who came.

0.2.n: The name of the country the speaker came to.

0.4.n: Plain past form of 来る, describing arrival before the time being discussed.

0.5.n: After a verb, 時 means the time when that action happens.

0.7.n: Names the season at the time of arrival.

0.8.n: The でし part of でした, the polite past form of です.

0.9.n: Completes でした, making the statement about autumn past tense.

1.0.n: Japanese month names use a number followed by 月.

1.1.n: Marks November as the time of arrival.

1.2.n: Plain past form of 来る, followed by a reason ending.

1.3.n: Connects the November arrival to the difficulty buying summer clothing.

1.5.n: The name of the country where the speaker tried to shop.

1.6.n: Marks Japan as the location of the attempted purchase.

1.7.n: Refers to items made for summer use, here pajamas.

1.8.n: Links 夏物 to パジャマ, specifying pajamas intended for summer.

1.9.n: A borrowed word written in katakana.

1.10.n: Sets summer pajamas as the topic of the negative statement.

1.11.n: Used with a negative verb to emphasize complete inability.

1.12.n: Polite past negative of 買える, the can-buy form of 買う.

2.0.n: The country name identifies where the stores are being compared.

2.1.n: Marks the location where Uniqlo exists.

2.2.n: Adds Singapore as another place with Uniqlo stores.

2.3.n: The name of a Japanese clothing retailer.

2.4.n: Highlights Uniqlo in contrast with GU.

2.5.n: Used for the presence of things or places, here a clothing store.

2.6.n: Short for の, adding explanatory background before です.

2.7.n: Makes the explanation polite as part of んです.

2.8.n: Introduces the contrast between having Uniqlo and not having GU.

2.10.n: Marks GU as the contrasting topic.

2.11.n: The linking form of ない, connecting GU’s absence to the following situation.

2.13.n: A casual filler that softens the description of the pajamas the speaker wanted.

2.14.n: The linking form of 可愛い, joining it to another description.

2.15.n: Describes a reasonable price; お adds a softer, more polished tone.

2.16.n: Connects お手頃 to the noun パジャマ.

2.17.n: The noun described by both 可愛くて and お手頃な.

2.18.n: Marks pajamas as the thing that could not be obtained.

2.19.n: Strengthens the negative expression that follows.

2.20.n: Part of 手に入る, an expression meaning to obtain or get hold of something.

2.21.n: Links 手 with 入る in the expression for getting hold of something.

2.22.n: Plain past negative of 入る; with 手に, it describes something not becoming obtainable.

2.23.n: Presents this difficulty as the reason for an action explained next.

3.1.n: The country name specifies which GU stores are meant.

3.2.n: Links Japan to GU, identifying GU stores located there.

3.4.n: Marks GU as the place where the pajamas went on sale.

3.5.n: Directly describes the pajamas without an extra linking word.

3.6.n: The item that GU began selling.

3.7.n: Marks pajamas as what was put on sale.

3.8.n: Plain past form of 売り出す, meaning to launch a product for sale, not necessarily discount it.

3.11.n: Connects the quoted announcement to 情報, identifying the information’s content.

3.12.n: Refers to the announcement about the new pajamas.

3.13.n: Marks the information as what the speaker saw.

3.14.n: Plain past form of 見る, here referring to seeing an announcement.

3.15.n: Links seeing the announcement to the decision to buy.

3.17.n: A common shortened form of インターネット.

3.18.n: Marks the internet as the means of purchasing.

3.19.n: The て-form of 買う links buying to the delivery action that follows.

3.20.n: Usually refers to the home where your parents or family live.

3.21.n: Marks the family home as the delivery destination.

3.22.n: Polite past form of 届ける; here the speaker arranged delivery rather than necessarily carrying the items personally.

4.0.n: A casual sentence connector used to continue the story.

4.2.n: Refers back to the pajamas; Japanese does not require a plural form here.

4.3.n: Marks the pajamas as what someone sent.

4.4.n: 送る in て-form plus もらいました shows the speaker received the favor of someone sending the pajamas.

0.lit: When I came to Singapore, it was autumn.
0.tip: A plain past verb before 時 forms a phrase meaning when that action happened.

1.lit: Because I came in November, as for summer pajamas, I could not buy any at all in Japan.
1.tip: 買えませんでした expresses past inability, not simply that the speaker did not buy something.

2.lit: In Singapore too, Uniqlo exists, but GU does not, and cute, affordable pajamas did not come into hand, so...
2.tip: 手に入る literally suggests coming into your hand, but means to get hold of something.

3.lit: Because I saw information saying GU in Japan started selling new pajamas, I bought online and delivered to family home.
3.tip: という links an announcement or quoted statement to a noun describing it, here 情報.

4.lit: And then, I received the favor of someone sending those.
4.tip: A verb in て-form plus もらう means someone does that action for your benefit.
